## Your team isn’t too busy to call. They’re too scared.

- Date: 25 April 2026
- Mirror: https://sidjashnani.com/blog/your-team-isnt-too-busy-to-call-theyre/
- Original: https://sidjashnani.substack.com/p/your-team-isnt-too-busy-to-call-theyre

Three calls. Five minutes. The habit your team won't do, and the lie they tell themselves about why

# Your team isn’t too busy to call. They’re too scared.

- Date: 25 April 2026
- Mirror: https://sidjashnani.com/blog/your-team-isnt-too-busy-to-call-theyre/
- Original: https://sidjashnani.substack.com/p/your-team-isnt-too-busy-to-call-theyre
- Author: Sid Jashnani, CEO of Outgrow and Outgrow Certified Advisor
- Type: Letter

Three calls. Five minutes. The habit your team won't do, and the lie they tell themselves about why

Every week, a founder tells me the same thing.

> “My team is too busy to call customers.”

Sometimes it’s “we don’t want to pester them.” Sometimes it’s “they’ll call us if they need something.” Sometimes it’s dressed up in the language of a busy operator: “we’re prioritising delivery.”

It’s the same answer every time. And it’s never the real reason.

The real reason your team isn’t picking up the phone has nothing to do with time. It’s fear. Until you accept that, no amount of CRM, training, or sales kickoff is going to move your revenue.

## The maths is offensive

Let me show you what “too busy” actually looks like.

Three proactive calls a day. Per person. That is the entire ask.

A proactive call, in the Outgrow system, is a call to a customer or prospect when nothing is wrong. No problem to fix. No urgent matter. You ring someone you have a relationship with and ask what they have coming up that you can help with. That’s it.

Three of those a day. Most go to voicemail. Most reps spend less than five minutes a day doing this work.

Five minutes. Per day.

If you have ten customer-facing people doing this, that’s 7,500 proactive conversations a year your business wasn’t having before. Two-thirds of those voicemails get a return communication when followed up with a text. That’s the Outgrow VM+Text technique, and the response rate holds up across 500+ companies and 100 million data points.

Five thousand return conversations from five minutes a day per person.

Tell me again how your team is too busy.

## The real objection

When a founder tells me the team doesn’t have time, I ask one question. “When was the last time you made one of these calls yourself?”

The answer is almost always the same. A long pause. Then some version of “it’s been a while.”

That’s the actual problem.

The team isn’t avoiding the calls because they’re busy. They’re avoiding them because nobody at the top is doing them. When the founder doesn’t make proactive calls, the team learns that proactive calls aren’t real work. The behaviour you tolerate is the behaviour you teach.

The other version of this objection, “we don’t want to pester our customers,” is just fear with better marketing.

Nobody is pestered by a five-minute call from someone they trust who asks if there’s anything they can help with. That isn’t pestering. That’s caring. Your customer doesn’t see your silence as respect. They see it as indifference. And when a competitor finally rings them, they answer.

## What the silence is actually costing you

Take your top twenty accounts. Ask yourself, honestly, what percentage of their relevant spend you currently hold. Not what you’d guess. What you actually know.

Most founders, when they push their team to find this number, get a brutal answer. Sometimes 5%. Sometimes less.

The other 95% is going to a competitor who is making the calls your team isn’t.

Three proactive calls a day per person, sustained for a year, is how that gap closes. Not a campaign. Not a quarterly push. A daily habit.

The companies adding 15 to 30% in revenue every year aren’t doing anything radical. They aren’t running clever campaigns. They’ve built one habit into their team’s day and protected it like sacred ground.

Five minutes. Three calls. Every day.

The maths works. The system works. The only question left is whether you’re willing to make the first call yourself, today, before you ask anyone else to.

That’s where it always starts.

## One thing to do this week

Pick three customers. Not prospects. Customers you already work with. People who would take your call.

Ring them. Leave a voicemail if they don’t pick up. Follow up with a text. Ask what they have coming up that you can help with.

If you can’t find five minutes for that, the problem isn’t your sales team.

## If You Know the Objection Is Coming, Why Are You Waiting For It?

- Date: 19 April 2026
- Mirror: https://sidjashnani.com/blog/if-you-know-the-objection-is-coming/
- Original: https://sidjashnani.substack.com/p/if-you-know-the-objection-is-coming

Why the best founders say it before anyone else does.

# If You Know the Objection Is Coming, Why Are You Waiting For It?

- Date: 19 April 2026
- Mirror: https://sidjashnani.com/blog/if-you-know-the-objection-is-coming/
- Original: https://sidjashnani.substack.com/p/if-you-know-the-objection-is-coming
- Author: Sid Jashnani, CEO of Outgrow and Outgrow Certified Advisor
- Type: Letter

Why the best founders say it before anyone else does.

A sales leader I respect told me a story recently that I have not stopped thinking about.

Early in his career, he gave a keynote to a room full of CEOs. Big companies. Experienced operators. People who had been running businesses for decades.

He got bad marks. Negative reviews.

The feedback? “There is nothing new in his talk.”

And he was furious. Not because the feedback was wrong. Because it was right. There was nothing new. But the whole point was that they already knew this stuff and were not doing it.

The problem was, he did not say that upfront. He let the audience sit there for an hour thinking they were hearing old news. By the time they left, the objection had already formed. Too late to fix it.

From that day forward, he addressed it on slide three. Before anyone had time to think “I already know this,” he told them: “You already know everything I am about to say. The question is whether you are doing it.”

The objection died in the room. Every time.

**Most founders wait for the pushback**

Think about the last time you introduced something new to your team. A new process. A new system. A new expectation.

You probably presented it, answered questions, and moved on. And then, three weeks later, you started hearing the resistance. “This does not work for us.” “We were already doing this.” “I do not see the point.”

By then, the damage is done. The objection has calcified into a belief. And beliefs are much harder to shift than reactions.

The fix is embarrassingly simple. If you know what they are going to push back on, say it first.

**Disarming the objection is strategy**

When you launch a new sales initiative with your team, you know exactly what is going to happen. They will start strong. Energy will fade. Some people will question whether it is working. Others will quietly stop doing the work and hope nobody notices.

You know this because it happens every time. With every team. In every company.

So why not say it out loud on day one?

“We are going to start strong. Then energy will dip. Some of you will wonder if this is worth the effort. That is completely normal. It happens in every company that does this. The difference between companies that grow and companies that stall is what happens after the dip.”

Now when the dip comes, it is not a crisis. It is a checkpoint. Something you predicted and prepared for.

**This applies everywhere, not just to internal initiatives**

Pricing conversations. Say the price is high before the client does. “This is not the cheapest option. Here is why it is the right one.”

Sales proposals. Name the risk before the buyer raises it. “You are probably wondering whether this will work for a company your size. Here is what happened with three companies exactly your size.”

Client onboarding. Tell them what the hard part will be before they hit it. “The first month will feel easy. Month three is where the real work starts. We will be here for that.”

In every case, you are doing the same thing. You are showing the other person that you understand their experience better than they do. That builds trust faster than any case study or testimonial.

**The question worth asking yourself this week**

What objection are you currently waiting to hear from your team, your clients, or your prospects that you already know is coming?

And what would change if you said it first?

Because the best sales leaders, the best founders, and the best account managers do not wait for the objection. They disarm it before it forms. And the conversation that follows is entirely different.

## Why I Still Believe in the Phone (And What a £20M Founder Said That Proved It)

- Date: 11 April 2026
- Mirror: https://sidjashnani.com/blog/why-i-still-believe-in-the-phone/
- Original: https://sidjashnani.substack.com/p/why-i-still-believe-in-the-phone

A proposal call, a healthcare clinic, and the one change that took response rates from 22% to 67%.

# Why I Still Believe in the Phone (And What a £20M Founder Said That Proved It)

- Date: 11 April 2026
- Mirror: https://sidjashnani.com/blog/why-i-still-believe-in-the-phone/
- Original: https://sidjashnani.substack.com/p/why-i-still-believe-in-the-phone
- Author: Sid Jashnani, CEO of Outgrow and Outgrow Certified Advisor
- Type: Letter

A proposal call, a healthcare clinic, and the one change that took response rates from 22% to 67%.

I was on a proposal call few weeks ago with the founder of a telecoms distribution business. £20M+ in revenue, built over decades. Sharp operator. Knows his market inside out.

We were about twenty minutes into talking about how his team could grow the B2B side of the business when he said something that stopped me.

“Young people can’t seem to talk on the phone anymore. But it’s the only real way to build relationships.”

He wasn’t complaining. He was diagnosing. And he was right.

His co-founder jumped in. They’d been talking about this internally for months. They’ve had salespeople come and go. Good people, not bad hires. But every time someone left, the customer relationships went with them. Nobody followed up. Nobody checked in. The accounts just went quiet until someone else eventually picked them up, if they picked them up at all.

And the people who stayed? They were doing the same thing most sales teams do. Sending emails. Sending quotes. Waiting for the phone to ring.

Not because they were lazy. Because calling feels risky. Email feels safe.

I’ve sat in enough of these conversations to know the pattern. The founder sees the problem clearly. The team knows it too. But nobody does anything about it because the alternative, picking up the phone and risking silence on the other end, feels worse than doing nothing.

Here’s the thing I’ve learned from working with companies on this exact issue: the fear isn’t about the phone. It’s about the response. Or the lack of one.

Your salesperson calls a customer. No answer. They feel like they’ve failed. They tried, right? Nobody picked up. So they mark it off and send an email instead.

But they called the wrong number. Or they called at the wrong time. Or they left a voicemail that sounded like every other voicemail from every other vendor. And then they gave up.

I worked with a healthcare clinic earlier this year that had this exact problem. They had appointment slots to fill, staff with the time and skill to help patients, and a booking system that was half empty. The team was sending text reminders and follow-up emails. Sensible. Professional. And completely ignored.

When I dug into what was happening, the answer was almost funny.

The clinicians and receptionists were calling patients on their mobiles, but they were calling from the clinic’s landline. And most people don’t pick up calls from numbers they don’t recognise these days. Especially landlines.

So the calls were going unanswered. Not because people didn’t want to talk. Because they saw an unknown number and ignored it.

We changed one thing. Call from a mobile phone instead of the clinic landline. If they don’t answer, leave a personal voicemail. Not a script. A real, human, 30-second message. Then follow up immediately with a text.

“Hi, it’s Rebecca from Dr. Williams’ practice. Just calling to check in after your last visit. Dr. Williams wanted to see if all is well with you and your recovery is on track. . Speak soon.”

Then the text: “Hi, this is Rebecca from Dr. Williams’ practice. Just left you a voicemail. Would Tuesday at 2pm or Thursday at 6pm work for a quick call to learn more about how you are recovering from xxxx?”

The response rate went from 22% to 67%.

Same patients. Same clinic. Same team. They just changed the channel and made it personal.

Now, here’s what the founder on my call last week wouldn’t have known yet, because we haven’t started working together. But I knew it the moment he described his team’s behaviour. The phone problem and the growth problem are the same problem.

His team has products their customers don’t know about. He admitted that openly. “Our existing customers aren’t being looked after as well as they could be.” His co-founder said they have “lots of products that potentially we could offer our customers.” But nobody is having those conversations.

Not because the products aren’t good. Not because the customers wouldn’t want them. Because the only way to have that conversation is on the phone, or face to face, or through a voice note on WhatsApp. And nobody is doing that because it feels uncomfortable.

This is the bit that I find endlessly fascinating about sales. The gap between what a company sells and what its customers know about is almost always a communication gap. Not a product gap. Not a marketing gap. A willingness-to-pick-up-the-phone gap.

In Europe and Asia, where I do a lot of my work, WhatsApp voice notes have become the modern equivalent of the voicemail. Your customer is on WhatsApp all day. A voicemail on your mobile may sit unheard for days. A voice note gets opened within minutes. Same principle. More relevant channel.

Either way, the point isn’t the technology. It’s the intention behind it. A personal voice message, whether it’s a voicemail or a WhatsApp note, says something that email never will: I thought about you specifically, and I picked up the phone to tell you.

That’s the whole game. That’s what the founder on my call was really saying. Relationships are built through voice. Through conversation. Through the willingness to be present with another person in real time, even if it’s just for 30 seconds on a recording.

His co-founder made a point that stuck with me too. He said most sales training only works for “the top 1% who have the knack.” Everyone else sits through the workshop, feels inspired for a day, and goes back to email by Monday.

He’s right. And that’s the trap. Most sales training teaches technique. But technique without habit is just a memory that fades. What you actually need is a system that makes the phone call the default, not the exception. Where logging the call, tracking the response, and following up becomes as automatic as checking your inbox in the morning.

That’s what I build with companies. Not a training day. A culture. Weekly tracking. Visible accountability. A set of simple questions that anyone in the business can ask. Not just the sales team. The ops people. The account managers. The project leads. Anyone who talks to a customer.

“Did you know we also handle endpoint security?” “What are you currently buying from someone else that we could help with?” “Who else at your company buys what you buy?”

These aren’t clever techniques. They’re obvious questions that nobody asks because nobody built the habit.

The founder I spoke with last week hasn’t signed up yet. He’s taking it to his board, doing the numbers, running through the costs with his finance director. That’s exactly what a smart operator does.

But here’s what I noticed during the call. About forty minutes in, he stopped asking me questions and started answering his own. “Why don’t I ask those DYK questions? It seems ridiculous we haven’t been asking.” His co-founder was nodding. They were selling each other on it.

That’s what happens when the solution is simple enough for everyone. It stops being a pitch and starts being a realisation.

The phone isn’t dead. Your team just needs a reason to use it. And a system that makes sure they keep using it long after the initial enthusiasm fades.

If that resonates, reply to this email. I’ll tell you exactly how the system works and what the first 90 days look like. No pitch deck. Just a conversation.

## Why Your Sales Pipeline Feels Like a Black Box

- Date: 19 March 2026
- Mirror: https://sidjashnani.com/blog/why-your-sales-pipeline-feels-like/
- Original: https://sidjashnani.substack.com/p/why-your-sales-pipeline-feels-like

How tracking inputs instead of outcomes creates predictable revenue

# Why Your Sales Pipeline Feels Like a Black Box

- Date: 19 March 2026
- Mirror: https://sidjashnani.com/blog/why-your-sales-pipeline-feels-like/
- Original: https://sidjashnani.substack.com/p/why-your-sales-pipeline-feels-like
- Author: Sid Jashnani, CEO of Outgrow and Outgrow Certified Advisor
- Type: Letter

How tracking inputs instead of outcomes creates predictable revenue

Most founders track revenue the same way.

Leads generated. Meetings booked. Proposals sent. Deals closed.

And then they sit back and wait. Hoping the numbers move.

But hope isn’t a strategy. And these metrics? They’re lagging indicators. By the time they tell you something’s wrong, it’s already expensive.

That’s why so many founders feel like they’re reacting to their business instead of running it.

A great quarter followed by a quiet one. Revenue that spikes and dips. No pattern. No predictability.

I’ve seen this over and over again.

**The Shift: Control the Controllables**

You can’t control when a customer decides to buy.

But you can control what your team does every single day.

This is the core idea behind the **[Outgrow](https://runoutgrow.com)** methodology — a system used by 500+ companies, backed by over 100 million data points.

Instead of tracking outcomes, you track Actions.

An “Action” isn’t just a phone call. It’s a complete system.

Here’s what one Action looks like:

1. You make a proactive call to a prospect or existing client.

2. If they don’t answer, you leave a voicemail.

3. You follow up with a text.

That’s one Action.

It’s not about dialling more numbers. It’s about completing the loop.

**Why Actions Work**

Most sales teams stop at the first attempt. No answer? Move on.

But the data tells a different story.

When you complete the full Action — call, voicemail, text — 66% of people respond.

These aren’t cold leads. They already know you. You’ve just not spoken in a while.

And when you layer in a simple question on the call — “Did you know we also offer this?” — 20% of the time, they buy something.

That’s 1 in 5.

Every five questions your team asks could turn into revenue, a quote, or a follow-up conversation.

The system works. But only if someone makes sure it actually happens.

**From Actions to Accountability**

Knowing this isn’t enough.

Most teams hear about proactive outreach and nod along. Then nothing changes.

That’s because Actions need a target. A rhythm. Accountability.

Here’s how to make it work:

𝟭. 𝗦𝗲𝘁 𝗮 𝘄𝗲𝗲𝗸𝗹𝘆 𝗔𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝘁𝗮𝗿𝗴𝗲𝘁.

Pick a number your team can commit to. Say, 500 Actions across the team per week.

𝟮. 𝗧𝗿𝗮𝗰𝗸 𝗶𝘁 𝘃𝗶𝘀𝗶𝗯𝗹𝘆.

Make it a scorecard. Review it every week. Celebrate progress. Address gaps.

𝟯. 𝗟𝗮𝘆𝗲𝗿 𝗶𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 “𝗗𝗶𝗱 𝗬𝗼𝘂 𝗞𝗻𝗼𝘄” 𝗾𝘂𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀.

Train your team to ask and stack multiple simple DYK questions on every call: “Did you know we also offer [X] or [Y] or [Z]?” - that’s 3 actions right there.

This isn’t selling. It’s helping. You’re reminding customers of value they might not know exists.

𝟰. 𝗔𝘀𝗸 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗿𝗲𝗳𝗲𝗿𝗿𝗮𝗹𝘀.

Once the relationship is warm, ask: “Who else do you know who might benefit from this?”

Most teams never ask. The ones who do grow faster.

**The Mindset Shift**

This isn’t just about process. It’s about belief.

Most salespeople avoid proactive calls because they think they’re bothering people.

They tell themselves:

- “If I call without an appointment, they’ll get upset.”

- “I should wait until I have something new to share.”

- “They’ll call me if they need something.”

That’s the voice of fear. And it kills momentum.

The truth is simpler.

They’re your customer. You’re calling to help them — not to bother.

When your team believes they’re adding value, they find a way to make the call.

When they believe they’re interrupting, they find excuses not to.

Mindset isn’t soft. It’s the foundation.

**The Gift of Predictable Revenue**

As go the inputs, so go the results.

There’s always a lag between the velocity of your Actions and the velocity of your revenue. But by systematically taking action, you’re not hoping for results. You’re engineering them.

You’re shortening the sales cycle.

You’re building the one thing most founders crave: predictability.

So here’s the question:

How many Actions did your team take last week?

Do you even know?

**If you’re a founder looking to build predictable sales operating system that actually works, I write about this every week in my newsletter, PREDICTABLE.**

## Why Your Sales Training Isn't Working

- Date: 27 February 2026
- Mirror: https://sidjashnani.com/blog/why-your-sales-training-isnt-working/
- Original: https://sidjashnani.substack.com/p/why-your-sales-training-isnt-working

The Optimism Advantage

# Why Your Sales Training Isn't Working

- Date: 27 February 2026
- Mirror: https://sidjashnani.com/blog/why-your-sales-training-isnt-working/
- Original: https://sidjashnani.substack.com/p/why-your-sales-training-isnt-working
- Author: Sid Jashnani, CEO of Outgrow and Outgrow Certified Advisor
- Type: Letter

The Optimism Advantage

Your pessimistic salespeople are costing you money.

Not because they’re bad at selling. Because pessimism kills action.

I’ve watched founders invest heavily in sales training. Objection handling workshops. Closing technique bootcamps. CRM systems. Scripts.

And then wonder why nothing changes.

The answer is usually simpler than they expect: their team’s heads are full of fear before they even pick up the phone.

---

## The COPE Mindset

I’ve been learning about this through my work as an [Outgrow Advisor](https://runoutgrow.com/advisor/sid-jashnani). Alex Goldfayn calls it COPE:

- **C** – Confidence
- **O** – Optimism
- **P** – Positivity
- **E** – Enthusiasm

You can’t fake these. And without them, every call becomes a burden.

Sales is two-thirds mindset. One-third technique.

Most companies get this backwards. They teach the technique and hope the mindset follows. It doesn’t.

---

## What the Research Says

[Recent research from Rockefeller University](https://x.com/aakashgupta/status/2025799591199969635?s=61) looked at the impact of optimism—not just on wellbeing, but on performance and longevity. The findings were striking:

- People in the most optimistic quartile lived **11-15% longer** (controlled for smoking, diet, exercise, alcohol, depression, and BMI)
- They had **50-70% higher odds** of reaching 85 years old
- **35% lower cardiovascular risk**
- Better stress management and faster emotional recovery

And here’s the part that matters for companies building sales teams:

**Optimistic sellers and business owners consistently outperform pessimistic ones.**

Not by a little. Significantly.

The research confirms what I’ve seen in the field: when your people believe good outcomes are possible, they act differently. They pick up the phone more. They follow up faster. They recover from rejection quicker.

Pessimism creates hesitation. Optimism creates momentum.

---

## The Skill Nobody Talks About

Here’s what most founders miss: **Optimism isn’t a fixed personality trait. It’s a learnable skill.**

You can train it. Just like you train objection handling or closing techniques.

This was the insight that shifted my thinking. We spend so much time trying to fix behaviours: call more, follow up faster, ask better questions, all without addressing the belief system underneath.

If someone believes “they probably won’t buy anyway,” no amount of technique will fix that. The fear shows up in their voice. Their prospects hear it before they finish the first sentence.

But if someone believes “this call could help them,” everything changes.

Same prospect. Different energy. Different outcome.

---

## How to Train Optimism

The research points to several practices that actually work:

**1. Cognitive Reappraisal**

This is the practice of reframing setbacks as temporary rather than permanent.

Instead of: “I lost that deal because I’m not good at this.” Try: “That deal didn’t close. What can I learn for the next one?”

The first interpretation creates paralysis. The second creates movement.

Train your team to catch themselves when they catastrophise. Ask them: “Is this a permanent truth, or a temporary setback?”

**2. Morning Sunlight**

This one surprised me. 10 minutes of natural light in the morning helps regulate mood and energy throughout the day.

It’s simple, free, and backed by science. Encourage your team to take calls outside or near a window in the morning. Small shift, real impact.

**3. Deliberate Breathing**

Before important calls, a few minutes of slow, controlled breathing calms the nervous system. [I particularly love box breathing. Try it on the Calm app.](https://www.calm.com/blog/box-breathing)

Fear shows up in the body first. Racing heart. Shallow breath. Tight shoulders. Your prospects can hear it.

A calm nervous system creates a calm voice. A calm voice creates trust.

**4. Structured Gratitude**

Write down 3 things you are grateful for daily - either when you wake up or before you sleep. Not goals. Not tasks.

This trains the brain to notice progress instead of problems. Over time, it shifts the default lens from “what’s wrong” to “what’s working.”

I’ve seen teams transform their energy within weeks of implementing this practice consistently.

---

## What Fear Sounds Like

You’ve probably heard these from your team:

- “If I call them, I’ll be bothering them.”
- “If I call without an appointment, they’ll get upset.”
- “I should wait until I have something new to share.”

That’s the voice of fear. And it’s contagious.

One pessimistic team member can drag down the energy of an entire sales floor. They don’t mean to. But negativity spreads faster than optimism.

The reframe is simple:

**They’re your customer. You’re there to serve them. When you pick up the phone, you’re calling to help—not to bother.**

That’s it.

When your salespeople believe that, COPE kicks in:

- Confidence replaces hesitation
- Optimism replaces dread
- Positivity replaces excuses
- Enthusiasm replaces avoidance

---

## Recognition Over Bonuses

One more insight from my recent learning: **recognition is more effective than money for driving behaviour change.**

Most founders default to bonuses and incentives. But recognition does something bonuses can’t:

- It’s public, so it teaches the rest of the team what good looks like
- It reinforces identity (”I’m someone who succeeds at this”)
- It motivates both the recipient and the observers

When someone on your team closes a deal or makes a great call, don’t just pay them more. Celebrate them publicly. Name the specific behaviour. Make it visible.

This builds optimism across the team, not just in one person.

---

## The Bottom Line

You can teach someone how to pitch. You can teach objection handling. You can teach closing.

But you can’t teach them to believe they’re helping people.

That belief has to come first.

If your sales feel inconsistent, if your team hesitates before picking up the phone, if rejection seems to linger longer than it should—the problem probably isn’t technique.

It’s mindset.

Fix that first. Then add the skills.

---

**One question to consider this week:**

Is your team’s mindset helping or hurting your sales?

---

*Sid*

*P.S. If you’re a leader stuck with unpredictable sales and want to build a system that creates predictable revenue growth, reply to this email. I’d be happy to share what’s working for my clients.*

Alex Goldfayn will walk through real Outgrow client case studies showing how companies add 15-30% in annual sales — predictably enough to hire and plan around it. Join us live March 2nd at 12 PM ET / 5 PM UK. [Save your spot.](https://runoutgrow.com/outgrow-predictable-sales-growth-webinar/)

## The 10 habits that separate bad bosses from great ones

- Date: 20 February 2026
- Mirror: https://sidjashnani.com/blog/the-10-habits-that-separate-bad-bosses/
- Original: https://sidjashnani.substack.com/p/the-10-habits-that-separate-bad-bosses

It’s not charisma or credentials — just 10 simple, repeatable habits that change everything.

# The 10 habits that separate bad bosses from great ones

- Date: 20 February 2026
- Mirror: https://sidjashnani.com/blog/the-10-habits-that-separate-bad-bosses/
- Original: https://sidjashnani.substack.com/p/the-10-habits-that-separate-bad-bosses
- Author: Sid Jashnani, CEO of Outgrow and Outgrow Certified Advisor
- Type: Letter

It’s not charisma or credentials — just 10 simple, repeatable habits that change everything.

## The 10 Habits That Separate Bad Bosses from Great Ones

I came across this visual today on LinkedIn and it nails the difference between bosses people *tolerate* and bosses people *follow*.

![Image from the essay “The 10 habits that separate bad bosses from great ones”](https://sidjashnani.com/assets/blog/the-10-habits-that-separate-bad-bosses/7c93168e4b44dd5d.webp)

It’s not personality.

It’s not degrees.

It’s habits.

Here’s the cheat sheet:

1. **Listens more than talks** → Great bosses absorb before they advise.
2. **Owns outcomes** → Doesn’t play the blame game. Ever.
3. **Shares context** → Gives people the *why*, not just the *what*.
4. **Has the hard talks** → Handles issues early, calmly, directly.
5. **Delegates decisions** → Trusts people to figure it out.
6. **Is consistent** → No mood swings, no surprises.
7. **Makes time** → Available, not just approachable.
8. **Reviews, not reacts** → Looks back quarterly, not emotionally.
9. **Says thank you** → Quickly, sincerely, specifically.
10. **Focuses forward** → Builds systems so the team can run without them.

The best bosses aren’t the loudest.

They’re the clearest.

They don’t need to “motivate” people.

Their habits *do* it for them.

---

**Bottom line:**

You don’t need to read another leadership or management book to become a great boss (though if you insist, *[How to Be a Great Boss](https://www.amazon.co.uk/How-Great-Boss-Gino-Wickman/dp/1942952848)*[by Gino Wickman](https://www.amazon.co.uk/How-Great-Boss-Gino-Wickman/dp/1942952848) won’t hurt your brain).

Just do these 10 things daily, consistently, almost obsessively.

Because leadership isn’t a chapter you read. It’s a muscle you train every day.

Until next week,

Sid

---

## How to Build Predictable Sales Without Carrying the Number

- Date: 30 January 2026
- Mirror: https://sidjashnani.com/blog/lbw-why-incentives-often-backfire/
- Original: https://sidjashnani.substack.com/p/lbw-why-incentives-often-backfire

A proven way to grow revenue without founder heroics

# How to Build Predictable Sales Without Carrying the Number

- Date: 30 January 2026
- Mirror: https://sidjashnani.com/blog/lbw-why-incentives-often-backfire/
- Original: https://sidjashnani.substack.com/p/lbw-why-incentives-often-backfire
- Author: Sid Jashnani, CEO of Outgrow and Outgrow Certified Advisor
- Type: Letter

A proven way to grow revenue without founder heroics

A founder said something to me recently that I cannot shake.

**“Take me out of the equation, and sales will collapse.”**

He was not proud of it. He was exhausted by it.

And I have heard versions of this sentence for seven years as a business coach. Different words. Same problem.

These were not broken companies.

Clear vision. Good people in the right seats. Strong accountability. Solid processes.

And yet sales still felt fragile. Personal. Founder dependent.

That question kept bothering me.

Why do some companies grow predictably, while others struggle every quarter?

---

## The pattern I kept seeing

The struggling companies were not lazy or incompetent.

They simply did not have a **system for sales**. They were banking on founder-led sales and their relationships or were waiting for their phone to ring.

They had systems for operations. Systems for finance. Systems for hiring.

But revenue was reactive.

Waiting for inbound leads. Hoping the pipeline fills. Leaning on the founder’s relationships to close deals.

Hope is not a strategy. I learned that painfully in my first two businesses.

The companies that grew consistently did one thing differently.

They took swings (actions) every single day. Not when things were desperate. Not at quarter end.

Daily. Relentless. Boring. Effective.

---

## Why I became an [Outgrow Certified Advisor](https://runoutgrow.com/advisor/sid-jashnani)

I believe deeply in every company implementing a business operating system. It gives companies clarity, structure, discipline, and execution.

But a business operating system does not fully solve sales.

It creates the structure around the business, accountabilities and processes. Revenue growth needs its own operating system.

That is where Outgrow fits.

Outgrow has been around for over 20 years under different names. More than 500 companies run on it.

The ones that commit to the work average **15–30% annual revenue growth**, year after year, as long as they run the system.

That is not a promise. That is a track record.

---

## What makes Outgrow different

**1. Sales is a habit, not a department.** Most companies outsource growth to the sales team or the founder. Outgrow involves every customer facing role. Everyone who touches a customer can create opportunity (or kill it).

**2. It is about doing, not training** I have sat through enough sales workshops that spike energy for a week and disappear. Outgrow is daily action. Choreographed work. Consistent swings.

**3. It creates positivity, not pressure** No fear tactics. No manipulation. Just habits that feel good and produce results. People want to do the work because they see it working.

---

## The math is simple

More swings (actions) equals more hits (revenue).

You cannot control who says yes. You **can** control how many conversations you start. How many follow ups you make. How many relationships you nurture.

> Control the controllables. Let the results follow.

That is the missing piece I was looking for.

---

## What this means for my work

I am still a coach helping you implement the world’s best business operating system. That does not change.

But now I can offer something I could not before. A proven way to build predictable revenue without the founder carrying the load.

If your sales feel inconsistent If you are tired of hoping next quarter will be different If you have ever thought “take me out and this falls apart”

I would love to talk.

No pitch. Just a real conversation about what is working and what is not.

---

## Want to see this system in action

I want to personally invite you to an upcoming live webinar hosted by my friend and founder of [Outgrow](http://runoutgrow.com)® **Alex Goldfayn**.

**Date/Time: 2-Feb-2026 at 5 PM UK (GMT)**

Alex will walk through the Outgrow system for predictable sales growth and show exactly how companies drive **15 to 30 percent organic revenue growth year after year** using proactive sales.

This is not theory. Outgrow is backed by 20 plus years of real world use and over **100 million data points**.

**In this session, you will learn:**

## Stop Tracking Results. Start Tracking Inputs

- Date: 2 January 2026
- Mirror: https://sidjashnani.com/blog/stop-tracking-results-start-tracking/
- Original: https://sidjashnani.substack.com/p/stop-tracking-results-start-tracking

Why great leaders manage inputs, not outcomes

# Stop Tracking Results. Start Tracking Inputs

- Date: 2 January 2026
- Mirror: https://sidjashnani.com/blog/stop-tracking-results-start-tracking/
- Original: https://sidjashnani.substack.com/p/stop-tracking-results-start-tracking
- Author: Sid Jashnani, CEO of Outgrow and Outgrow Certified Advisor
- Type: Letter

Why great leaders manage inputs, not outcomes

I teach leaders how to make faster, clearer decisions.

And yet, for years, I relied on my gut and got it wrong about half the time.

High stakes decisions. Big consequences. Made on intuition. Ego. Experience.

A coin toss.

Sometimes it worked. Sometimes it blew up.

That is not strategy. That is gambling.

---

## The Realisation

Intuition is not the problem.

Unfiltered intuition is.

Most founders overtrust their gut because it feels decisive. Confident. Leader like.

But confidence without data is just guesswork with better posture.

So I learned to add data behind the madness.

---

## The Shift That Changed Everything

For every business or division, I now run a weekly scorecard and monthly P&L review.

Not a vanity dashboard. Not lagging results.

A simple weekly scorecard focused on **inputs**.

Not revenue this month But sales calls made.

Not new clients won But proposals sent.

Not utilisation achieved But client meetings held.

These are the only things I can truly control.

---

## Why Inputs Matter More Than Outputs

Outputs are history. Inputs are leverage.

If you obsess over outcomes, you react. If you manage inputs, you lead.

When inputs are strong and consistent, results usually follow. When results are weak, the scorecard tells me exactly where the breakdown is.

No emotion. No ego. No storytelling.

Just signal.

---

## Intuition Still Has a Seat at the Table

I have not abandoned instinct.

I have disciplined it.

Intuition is a hypothesis. The scorecard is the test.

Together, they give me clarity on three decisions every week:

- Go
- No go
- Pivot

That is how you raise your batting average as a leader.

---

## The Leadership Question

Most leaders are obsessing over outputs they cannot directly control.

While ignoring the inputs that actually drive them.

So I will leave you with this:

**What inputs are you ignoring while obsessing over outcomes?**

Because if you do not manage the inputs, the business will manage you.

Until next week, Sid

## LBW: The 3 Mistakes Founders Make with Offshore Teams

- Date: 28 November 2025
- Mirror: https://sidjashnani.com/blog/lbw-the-3-mistakes-founders-make/
- Original: https://sidjashnani.substack.com/p/lbw-the-3-mistakes-founders-make

Most founders make these and they’re easy to fix.

# LBW: The 3 Mistakes Founders Make with Offshore Teams

- Date: 28 November 2025
- Mirror: https://sidjashnani.com/blog/lbw-the-3-mistakes-founders-make/
- Original: https://sidjashnani.substack.com/p/lbw-the-3-mistakes-founders-make
- Author: Sid Jashnani, CEO of Outgrow and Outgrow Certified Advisor
- Type: Podcast

Most founders make these and they’re easy to fix.

Hiring offshore can save you 60–70% in costs. But most founders still struggle to get results. Why? Because they unknowingly make the same three mistakes over and over again.

---

## Mistake #1: Treating Them Like Outsiders

You can’t build trust with distance.

Too many leaders treat their offshore staff as “vendors” or “assistants” instead of teammates.

The fix is simple:

- Welcome them like you would an in-office hire.
- Introduce them to the team on Day 1.
- Share your story, your culture, your rituals.

Belonging drives performance. Not payroll.

---

## Mistake #2: Dumping Tasks Without Context

I see this all the time. An offshore team member logs in for the first time and within 20 minutes, they’re handed a monster task.

They’re nervous. They don’t know your culture or expectations yet. They just joined.

Ease them in. Start with simple wins that build confidence and rhythm. Then scale responsibility as trust builds.

---

## Mistake #3: Ghosting on Communication

No meetings. No check-ins. No feedback. Just silence and Slack pings.

Communication isn’t optional, it’s the oxygen of remote teams. Start with:

- A **daily 10-minute huddle** (even async updates work)
- A **weekly one-on-one** to align expectations and coach performance
- Make them part of the correct departmental or appropriate Level 10 meeting.

Your offshore people don’t need micromanagement. They need presence.

---

## The Bottom Line

Treat them like insiders. Onboard them properly. Communicate like clockwork.

Do this, and your offshore team will perform as if they’re right across the hall not across the ocean.

Until next week, **Sid**

---

**P.S.** Thinking of hiring offshore? We’ve helped dozens of founders build world-class remote teams that deliver results. Reply to the email and share what kind of role you’re looking to delegate so we can help you hire the right person in the right seat.

## LBW: The Hard Truth About Leadership & Friendship

- Date: 24 November 2025
- Mirror: https://sidjashnani.com/blog/lbw-the-hard-truth-about-leadership/
- Original: https://sidjashnani.substack.com/p/lbw-the-hard-truth-about-leadership

Being liked feels good. Being respected gets results

# LBW: The Hard Truth About Leadership & Friendship

- Date: 24 November 2025
- Mirror: https://sidjashnani.com/blog/lbw-the-hard-truth-about-leadership/
- Original: https://sidjashnani.substack.com/p/lbw-the-hard-truth-about-leadership
- Author: Sid Jashnani, CEO of Outgrow and Outgrow Certified Advisor
- Type: Letter

Being liked feels good. Being respected gets results

So there I was, sitting across from a founder who’d built a $3.5M business from scratch. Smart, driven, and utterly miserable.

“What’s the biggest problem in your business right now?” I asked.

His answer? “No one does what they’re supposed to do unless I micromanage them.”

As we dug deeper, the real issue emerged: **He was trapped in the friendship zone with his entire leadership team.**

## The Friendship Trap

Here’s a confession: I’ve fallen into this trap myself (multiple times, because I’m a slow learner).

At Momentum Group, I once had a senior VP who:

- Missed deadlines regularly
- Delivered subpar work
- Created team drama

And what did I do? Schedule “feedback sessions” that turned into friendly chats about sports, family, and weekend plans. We’d end with vague promises to “do better next time.”

Guess what happened? Nothing improved. For months.

Why? Because I prioritised being liked over being respected.

## The Accountability Problem

Patrick Lencioni nails it in his book “The Five Temptations of a CEO” when he identifies one of the deadliest leadership sins:

“Wanting to be popular with your direct reports instead of holding them accountable.”

This isn’t just a rookie mistake—it’s an epidemic among even seasoned leaders.

The hard truth: **Your job isn’t to be their friend. It’s to help them become their best.**

And sometimes, that means having uncomfortable conversations.

## Signs You’re Too Deep in the Friendship Zone:

- You avoid giving negative feedback
- You let deadlines slide without consequences
- You spend more time talking about personal life than performance
- You worry about “hurting feelings” when discussing work issues
- You have the same improvement conversation multiple times

Sound familiar? Don’t worry, you’re in good company (mine).

## The Reset Button

After watching my business suffer, I finally hit reset:

- **Clear Expectations**: I documented exactly what success looked like for each role
- **Regular Check-ins**: Scheduled weekly one-on-ones focused primarily on metrics and goals
- **Direct Feedback**: Delivered within 24 hours, good or bad
- **Real Consequences**: Made it clear that continued underperformance wasn’t an option

The results? Two team members stepped up dramatically. One chose to leave. And my business grew 28% the following year.

## Finding Balance

This doesn’t mean becoming a cold, distant boss. In fact, the best leader-team relationships involve:

- Genuine care for your people’s growth
- Deep understanding of their strengths and weaknesses
- Investment in their development
- Respectful, direct communication

As one of my mentors put it: “Be friendly, not friends.”

## The Bottom Line

The kindest thing you can do for your team isn’t protecting their feelings—it’s helping them grow through honest feedback and clear expectations.

Your team doesn’t need another friend. They need a leader.

Until next week,

Sid

P.S. What’s your experience with this balance? Reply and let me know—I read every response.

*Know a leader struggling with this balance? Forward this email. They’ll either thank you or never speak to you again. Either way, problem solved!*

---

## LBW: Want your team to change? You first.

- Date: 22 November 2025
- Mirror: https://sidjashnani.com/blog/lbw-want-your-team-to-change-you/
- Original: https://sidjashnani.substack.com/p/lbw-want-your-team-to-change-you

The embarrassing lesson I learned about walking the talk.

# LBW: Want your team to change? You first.

- Date: 22 November 2025
- Mirror: https://sidjashnani.com/blog/lbw-want-your-team-to-change-you/
- Original: https://sidjashnani.substack.com/p/lbw-want-your-team-to-change-you
- Author: Sid Jashnani, CEO of Outgrow and Outgrow Certified Advisor
- Type: Letter

The embarrassing lesson I learned about walking the talk.

TLDR: Your company initiatives are failing because you (yes, YOU) aren’t following them. Ask me how I know.

2015: I went full Tony Robbins.

- Dropped $$$ on leadership programs and exec education
- Filled notebooks with “game-changing” frameworks
- Bought enough business books to start a library
- Almost got a “hustle harder” tattoo (kidding... maybe)

My company, Momentum, was scaling fast. $4M → $35M.

But here’s the thing about scaling...

It’s like trying to build a plane while flying it. Except I was the pilot telling everyone else to follow the manual while freestyling my own moves

## The Leadership Trap

Quick story time:

Me in meetings: “Guys, we NEED systems and processes!” Also me: *hasn’t updated my scorecard in 3 weeks*

Me to team: “No phones in Level 10 meetings!” Also me: *sending emails under the table like a high schooler texting in math class*

Me on processes: “Follow the system!” Also me: “But this deal is different...”

Notice a pattern?

## Rules Don’t Apply To Me

Know what happens when the founder plays by different rules?

- Trust dies faster than my New Year’s resolutions
- Eye rolls become an Olympic sport
- “Yes boss” becomes code for “whatever you say, buddy”
- New initiatives are treated like crypto in 2024

## The Numbers Don’t Lie

In departments where we actually followed the system:

- Project completion: ⬆️ 40%
- Chaos: ⬇️ 80%
- Hair pulling: ⬇️ 90%

But because I kept making “founder exceptions,” we couldn’t scale it.

## The Wake-Up Call

Every Monday at 10am, L10 time. The rules were crystal clear:

- No phones
- To-dos completed
- Scorecard updated
- Issues list prepped

Me at 10:07am, typing on my phone: “Sorry team, client emergency. Keep going, I’m listening...”

Until one Monday my Integrator just stood up: “Let’s cancel today. We’ll restart when you’re ready to play by your own rules.”

## The Fix

Want your company to actually change?

- Do the thing
- Keep doing the thing
- No “special founder circumstances”
- Seriously, just keep doing the thing

That’s it. That’s the newsletter.

When I finally started eating my own dog food

- Meetings got shorter
- Decisions got faster
- Problems got solved
- My blood pressure dropped

## The Bottom Line

Stop being the “rules for thee but not for me” founder. (Trust me, your team already has a group chat about it)

Keep it real,

Sid

P.S. I still have those 2015 notebooks. They’re great for propping up my monitor. At least they’re supporting something.

*Know a leader who preaches process but plays by different rules? Forward this email. Their team already has a group chat about it.*

---

## LBW: Your Indecision Is Costing You (More Than You Think)

- Date: 19 November 2025
- Mirror: https://sidjashnani.com/blog/lbw-your-indecision-is-costing-you/
- Original: https://sidjashnani.substack.com/p/lbw-your-indecision-is-costing-you

That decision you're avoiding? It's getting expensive.

# LBW: Your Indecision Is Costing You (More Than You Think)

- Date: 19 November 2025
- Mirror: https://sidjashnani.com/blog/lbw-your-indecision-is-costing-you/
- Original: https://sidjashnani.substack.com/p/lbw-your-indecision-is-costing-you
- Author: Sid Jashnani, CEO of Outgrow and Outgrow Certified Advisor
- Type: Letter

That decision you're avoiding? It's getting expensive.

Ever watched a leader take 3 months to make a 3-minute decision?

I have. Multiple times. (I was that leader once).

## The Discussion Trap

Here’s what I see in almost every leadership team meeting:

An issue comes up. Everyone jumps straight to discussing it:

- “We should look into...”
- “Maybe we could try...”
- “What if we considered...”

45 minutes later, nobody has actually identified what the real issue is and they’ve probably gone off tangent by now.

Why? Because identifying the real issue often reveals an uncomfortable truth that requires a tough decision. And tough decisions are, well... tough.

## Real Talk

Last month, I watched a tech company CEO spend 6 weeks “discussing” an underperforming sales manager. Meeting after meeting. Report after report.

The actual issue? The CEO knew this person needed to go but was afraid of making the call. He was hoping that the issue would solve itself.

Cost of all that “discussion”? $42,000 in salary for subpar work, plus a demoralised team watching their leader avoid the obvious.

## Breaking The Cycle

Want to know if you’re stuck in the discussion trap? Watch out for these phrases:

- “Let’s take this offline” (Translation: Never)
- “We need more data” (Translation: I’m scared to decide)
- “Let’s circle back next week” (Translation: Hope everyone forgets)

If you genuinely need more information or a dedicated discussion, then make a real decision right now: Get that meeting on the calendar. Be specific about who’s bringing what data. Then come back next week ready to move forward with a clear plan.

## The 24 Hour Rule

Try this: Any issue that lands on your desk gets 24 hours. Within that time, you must:

- Name the real issue (not the symptom)
- Make a decision - can be just the next step.
- Take action

Yes, even the tough ones. Especially the tough ones.

Will you make mistakes? Sure.

Will they cost less than weeks of indecision? Almost always.

## Your Challenge This Week

Pick that one issue you’ve been “discussing” for weeks.

You know the one. Name it. Decide. Act.

Do it before this time tomorrow.

Then email me and tell me how it felt.

Until next week,

**Sid**

P.S. Fun fact: I spent 20 minutes debating whether this P.S. was funny enough to include. The irony is not lost on me.

*Know a leader stuck in the discussion loop? Forward this their way. Their team will thank you.*

---

## LBW: Most underrated way to get what you want

- Date: 27 October 2025
- Mirror: https://sidjashnani.com/blog/lbw-most-underrated-way-to-get-what/
- Original: https://sidjashnani.substack.com/p/lbw-most-underrated-way-to-get-what

Everyone wants something. This ONE thing will help you achieve your goals.

# LBW: Most underrated way to get what you want

- Date: 27 October 2025
- Mirror: https://sidjashnani.com/blog/lbw-most-underrated-way-to-get-what/
- Original: https://sidjashnani.substack.com/p/lbw-most-underrated-way-to-get-what
- Author: Sid Jashnani, CEO of Outgrow and Outgrow Certified Advisor
- Type: Letter

Everyone wants something. This ONE thing will help you achieve your goals.

Want to know the superpower that will define business success in 2026?

It’s not AI.

It’s not Elon or Donald.

It’s not even having a fancy LinkedIn title with “Thought Leader” in it (even though that would be cool to get - and I know some of my subscribers already have it).

It’s something so basic, so fundamental, that it’s almost embarrassing to write about.

## The Secret? Do What You Say

That’s it. That’s the newsletter.

(Just kidding, keep reading...)

Here’s what’s wild: This used to be the bare minimum to do business. The absolute baseline. Now? It’s become a superpower. An actual competitive advantage.

We’re living in an epidemic of unfulfilled promises:

- “I’ll get back to you tomorrow” (They didn’t)
- “Let’s circle back next week” (Translation: Let’s pretend this conversation never happened)
- “It’s at the top of my priority list” (Right below scrolling Instagram for 3 hours)
- “Your call is important to us” (But not important enough to hire more people)

## The Maths Is Simple

If you consistently do what you say:

- You’re automatically better than 99.9% of your competition
- Your customer satisfaction scores will skyrocket
- Your team will trust you
- Your business will grow

Not because you’re doing anything revolutionary. But because you’re doing something that’s become revolutionary by its scarcity: Following through.

## That’s it

No frameworks. No complicated strategies. No 12-step processes.

Yet somehow we’ve created a business world where:

- 5 follow-up emails is “normal”
- “ASAP” means “whenever I get around to it”
- And “end of day” could mean any day in the next quarter

The solution?

**Just do what you say.**

Your customers will think you’re a unicorn.

Your team will think you’re a genius.

Your competition will wonder what your secret is.

And you’ll be sitting there knowing that your “competitive advantage” is simply keeping your word.

Until next week,

**Sid**

P.S. I promised this would be a short newsletter. Look at me, doing what I say.

*If you know someone who needs this reminder (we all do), share this post. I promise it’ll help. And yes, that’s a promise I intend to keep.*
